questions.q: Which `cmdb_ci` subclass is used for SCHED-SQL-01, the CI hosting the scheduling database?
options: cmdb_ci_appl
cmdb_ci_lb_device
cmdb_ci_db_instance
cmdb_ci_win_server
questions.explain: SCHED-SQL-01 is a SQL Server instance, modeled with cmdb_ci_db_instance — a different subclass than the servers (cmdb_ci_win_server) or the application (cmdb_ci_appl).

questions.q: What relationship type connects Patient Scheduling App to SCHED-APP-01 and SCHED-APP-02?
options: Sends Data To
Load Balances
Runs on
Depends on
questions.explain: The application runs on both servers, using the Runs on relationship type. Depends on connects the servers to the database instance.

questions.q: Why does documenting SCHED-APP-01's and SCHED-APP-02's Depends on relationship to SCHED-SQL-01 matter most for impact analysis?
options: It doesn't matter — the load balancer relationship is the only one that affects impact analysis
It shows that a maintenance event on the shared database affects both app servers, and the application, even with no change made to either server
It only matters for billing purposes, not for impact analysis
Database relationships are never relevant to impact analysis
questions.explain: Because both servers depend on the one database instance, maintenance on SCHED-SQL-01 ripples upward to both servers and the application, even though neither server itself changes.

questions.q: How is the connection to the EHR platform documented in this capstone?
options: By creating full CI records for the EHR platform's servers and database
It is left undocumented entirely, since the EHR is out of scope
By adding one relationship — Patient Scheduling App Sends Data To the existing EHR Integration Service — without creating new CIs for the EHR side
By merging Patient Scheduling App and the EHR platform into a single CI
questions.explain: The scope boundary from Lesson 23 holds: one relationship documents the real connection without taking on infrastructure this capstone doesn't own.

questions.q: Why is SCHED-LB-01's relationship to each app server documented explicitly rather than left implied?
options: Load balancer relationships cannot be represented in the CMDB at all
So an administrator looking at SCHED-LB-01 alone can see exactly which servers it distributes traffic to
Because load balancers are never relevant to a dependency view
It is only required for database CIs, not for load balancers
questions.explain: A CI's relationships should be visible from that CI's own record — assuming a reader already knows the topology defeats the purpose of documenting it.
